audit.why: HARD at 7/10 matches 47.67% over 1628 games — the largest sample on the page. Decisive Strike is an 8-second silence that also resets his auto, and a silenced Sejuani cannot cast Winter's Wrath or Permafrost, which is her whole pattern. The lane is conceded and reclaimed after two items.
audit.corrected: Difficulty and the Garen-favoured early chart kept.

audit.whatIsWrong: whys[3] states 'Courage cooldown is shorter than your full rotation reset', which is used to argue no window exists at levels 4-5.
audit.why: Courage is 22/19.5/17/14.5/12s; Arctic Assault is 18/16.5/15/13.5/12s. At rank 1 his W is four seconds LONGER than your Q, and they only converge at rank 5. The window exists early and closes late — the exact opposite of what the page says, and it changes when you are supposed to fight.
audit.corrected: Rewritten as a window that exists at low ranks and narrows as he levels W.

audit.whatIsWrong: Three misses. (a) Courage is described only as absorbing burst. (b) Decisive Strike's slow-cleanse is never mentioned. (c) 'your passive Permafrost resistances' fuses Permafrost with Fury of the North's Frost Armor.
audit.why: Riot on Courage: 'activate this ability to give him a shield and tenacity for a brief moment followed by a lesser amount of damage reduction' — the tenacity directly shortens your Permafrost stun and your Glacial Prison stun, which is a bigger problem for a CC tank than the shield is. Riot on Decisive Strike: 'Garen gains a burst of Move Speed, breaking free of all slows affecting him' — Winter's Wrath's slow and Glacial Prison's storm slow simply come off him, so slow-based kiting does not exist in this matchup. Riot on Fury of the North: the resistances are Frost Armor, granted out of combat; Permafrost is a 1.5s stun at max Frost stacks and grants nothing defensive.
audit.corrected: Tenacity stated wherever Courage is discussed; the slow-cleanse stated in early and wants.foe[2]; Frost Armor named correctly in late and whys[6].

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns gives Courage no number and never mentions Decisive Strike, the ability that actually breaks your combo.
audit.why: Courage 22/19.5/17/14.5/12s, Decisive Strike 8s flat at 300 range, Judgment 9/8.25/7.5/6.75/6s, Demacian Justice 120/100/80s.
audit.corrected: Both numbers written in, with the slow-cleanse attached to the 8-second clock.

audit.why: The stated win condition — survive to two tank items and shrink the missing-health window Demacian Justice executes from — is sound: Riot types R as an execute, so raw HP is the correct counter and Heartsteel is the correct item.
audit.corrected: Kept, with the execute mechanic stated explicitly rather than implied.

edits.before: Land Q knock-up outside Courage's active window, then immediately chain W-W into E Permafrost stun before he can regen

edits.after: Garen owns levels 1 through 3: Decisive Strike is an 8-second silence at 300 range that also resets his auto, and Perseverance regenerates whatever chip you land. Take W first, walk the wave, and only step inside 300 if you can knock him up first — silenced, you cannot cast Winter's Wrath or Permafrost at all. His Q also breaks free of every slow on him, so Winter's Wrath will not keep him off you. Zero deaths and Heartsteel stacks, not lane pressure.
edits.before: Garen owns levels 1 through 3 cleanly: his Q silence interrupts your W mid-animation and his passive regen erases whatever chip damage you land before you can follow up. Take W first, walk the wave, and do not step into his Q range unless you can immediately throw your own Q knock-up — you need him airborne before he silences you or Courage will eat your whole combo. Your goal is zero deaths and Heartsteel stacks, not lane pressure.

edits.after: The lane stays contested through 4 and 5 — Courage's shield and tenacity blunt your stun and Perseverance outheals your poke between fights, so fight only while Decisive Strike's 8 seconds is running and your full Q-W-W-E chain is ready. Level 6 is the real inflection point: Glacial Prison starts the fight from beyond his 300-range silence, so the CC lands before Courage is up rather than into it. Throw R first — walking in with Q hands him the silence and the auto reset.
edits.before: The lane stays contested through levels 4 and 5 — Garen's Courage still cuts your E stun damage and his regen outheals your poke between fights, so fight only when his Q Decisive Strike is on cooldown and your full Q-W-W-E chain is ready. Level 6 is your real inflection point: Glacial Prison lets you initiate from outside his Silence range, CC him before Courage activates, and run the full stun chain — the window exists, but you need to throw R first rather than walking in with Q.

edits.after: Two tank items later the matchup inverts. Frost Armor from Fury of the North makes you effectively unkillable in the side lane, and Demacian Justice executes off missing health, so every point of HP you stack shrinks the window where his R is lethal. Play around Dragon and Baron, use Glacial Prison to lock the fight, and you become the win condition. The 1v1 is yours, and a single 8-second silence cannot answer your teamfight CC chain.
edits.before: Two tank items later the matchup inverts completely. Your passive Permafrost resistances make you effectively unkillable in the side lane and Garen's Demacian Justice execute loses its value as your HP pool climbs — he cannot generate enough missing-HP on you to make R lethal. Play around Dragon and Baron, use Glacial Prison to lock the fight, and you become the win condition. The 1v1 is yours and your teamfight CC chain is something Garen cannot answer with a single silence.

edits.after: - Garen Courage (22/19.5/17/14.5/12s): matchup-defining — the shield eats your burst and its tenacity shortens your stun. - Decisive Strike is 8s: it silences at 300 and breaks every slow off him. - Your Q is 18s; hold R for the fight that decides something.
edits.before: - Garen Courage: matchup-defining — Damage reduction on cast — your burst only lands full once it is down. It governs your forward steps. - Q dash spent on poke is a death you scheduled. - Hold the R for the fight that decides something.

edits.after: Frost stacks decide every trade: fight only with the full Q-W-E chain up and Courage's 22 seconds still running.
edits.before: Frost stacks decide every trade: fight only when the full Q-W-E chain is available. Track Courage before stepping up.

edits.after: - Sejuani vs Garen - Track: Courage, 22s — shield plus tenacity. - His Q breaks your slows. - Fights start when Decisive Strike is spent. - The R is for endings.
edits.before: - Sejuani vs Garen - Track: Garen Courage. - Trade only through full Permafrost chains. - Fights start when Courage ends. - The R is for endings, not openings.

notes: The single most useful fact this page was missing: Decisive Strike 'breaks free of all slows affecting him' (Riot's own wording). Sejuani's Winter's Wrath slow and the Glacial Prison storm slow are both cleansed by an 8-second basic ability, which means slow-based kiting and zoning do not function in this matchup at all. Second: Courage grants tenacity, not just a shield — for a champion whose entire win condition is stun duration, that is the more important half of the ability and it appeared nowhere. Third, the recurring site-wide error again: 'passive Permafrost resistances' (late) and 'your passive resistances' fuse Permafrost with Fury of the North's Frost Armor. Worth a global grep for 'Permafrost passive' and 'passive Permafrost' across champ-data/content/sejuani.js and champ-data/sejuani.full.js — it appears on at least four Sejuani pages in this slice.
